What is Kant's synthetic a priori, and how is it supposed to solve Humean skepticism?

So synthetic judgments are basically things that are contingently true. "The coffee mug is on the table" may be true, but that's true only based on the particular configuration of items.

A priori judgments are any judgments which contain some sort of knowledge which must be known a priori to existence. To Kant, causation is an example of this. You don't get an idea of causation by experiencing the world, you must have an idea of causation a priori before the world can be understood. This is the typical form of a transcendental argument.

So with the synthetic a priori, Kant asks, "Can we combine our concepts with our a priori concepts and form new knowledge?" in a non-tautological sense. He answers yes, which would mean we can know something without having to experience that something. But good examples for this are hard to come by.

Don't assume this is negative, just hear me out: We're at this phase in bitcoin development where we keep waiting for the embers to catch on fire, but it hasn't seemed to happen yet. Bitcoin and blockchain technology are certainly real - we've passed the phase where people might assume bitcoin is vaporware, but adoption is still slow. When we look at the adoption of the internet, there was simply nothing that could provide the same feature set, so when people discovered the power of networking they had an instant "Aha!" moment when they sent an email, went to a website, or played a networked game. On the contrary, the transition from IPv4 to IPv6 has been much slower, though obviously necessary. Users aren't generally ecstatic about the transition because their existing model works - even though many of us recognize its days are numbered. We can see that IPv6 and bitcoin are likely the technologies that will dominate in the future, but I no longer expect the sweeping and dramatic adoption that I thought we would see. Bitcoin does bring new features to money, but most people will view the transition to bitcoin as an incremental upgrade rather than a new way of doing business - I suspect it will take many more years for people to grasp the full impact that bitcoin and blockchains will have on the world of currency.
People often say the adoption of bitcoin will follow the adoption pattern of the Internet - I think it will follow the adoption curve of IPV6
